solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Torch is initially held for waving (8)

annotation.definitionNote: BRANDISH is read as a noun, a flourish or wave, to match 'waving'

indicatorNotes.initially: takes the first letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: a brand is a burning stick, a torch

annotation.surface: Someone holds a torch aloft to wave it about, signalling or celebrating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Torch' looks like the thing being waved, but it is BRAND, an old word for a burning stick.
annotation.definitionFit: A brandish is a flourishing wave of something held in the hand.

entries.clue: Cheese: artist devours it when circling function (7)

indicatorNotes.devours: RA takes the rest inside itself, as a mouth takes food
indicatorNotes.circling: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so IT surrounds the function

annotation.surface: A painter tucks into cheese while at some social function.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, the inner one built first. 'Function' suggests a party to go with the cheese; it is the trigonometry kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

entries.clue: Demand from cineaste: set to be rebuilt (11)

indicatorNotes.to be rebuilt: the letters are put back together in a new order

annotation.surface: A fussy film director insists the film set be torn down and rebuilt.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a film buff's demand about a set; 'set' is simply three more letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a situation that makes something unavoidable demands it.

entries.clue: Horrified grimace right away showing stress (5)

indicatorNotes.away: the R is sent away from the word

blocks.note: a rictus is a fixed, gaping grimace, as of horror

annotation.surface: A face frozen in horror betrays how much stress someone is under.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stress' looks like nervous strain, but ICTUS is the stress on a syllable in verse.
annotation.definitionFit: An ictus is the rhythmical stress in a line of verse.

entries.clue: Weary remark from drunk taken around English house (5-2)

indicatorNotes.taken around: to take something around is to carry it about you, so the drunk encloses English

annotation.surface: A tipsy person is steered home, sighing wearily on the way.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface picture of a drunk being escorted home hides a container; 'house' as HO is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is an exclamation of weariness or resignation.

entries.clue: Heathen almost incarcerates old duke in temple (6)

indicatorNotes.incarcerates: to incarcerate is to imprison, so the shortened heathen holds the old duke inside

annotation.surface: An irreligious captor locks up an elderly nobleman inside a place of worship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost' acts first, trimming the heathen before the prisoner goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered temple of East Asia.

entries.clue: Blackball news boss: paper giving unrealistic hope (4,5)

blocks.note: to pip is to blackball, to reject by ballot
a ream is a quantity of paper

annotation.surface: Someone who snubs a newspaper editor imagines their paper will then offer them hope.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like the newspaper again; it is a ream of paper, a stationery quantity.
annotation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fanciful hope that will never come true.

entries.clue: Swimmer seen in Ghasri periodically (3)

annotation.surface: A swimmer is spotted at intervals in some place called Ghasri.
annotation.walkthrough: Ghasri is there only to carry the letters: G, A, R, skipping h, s and i.
annotation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted fish, so a swimmer.

entries.clue: Outing Democrat — one in beaten party (3,4)

indicatorNotes.in: I goes inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.beaten: PARTY is knocked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A Democrat is outed as a member of the party that lost the election.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outing' looks like exposing someone; it is an excursion. 'Beaten party' sounds like the losing side at an election.
annotation.definitionFit: A day trip is a short outing there and back in a day.

entries.clue: Queue to leave when stuck in bumptious social gathering? (8,5)

indicatorNotes.stuck in: TAIL and PART are put inside COCKY

blocks.note: a tail is a line of people or cars, a queue

annotation.surface: At a pompous gathering, a guest wants to leave but is stuck in the queue.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a guest trapped in a line at a pompous do; the question mark admits the definition is a little broad.
annotation.definitionFit: A cocktail party is a social gathering where drinks are served.

entries.clue: Dreaded police succeeded in state allowing no change (6)

blocks.note: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police
s. = succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A feared secret police force has seized power in a state where nothing ever changes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country, matching the police; it is a condition.
annotation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium or inactivity where nothing changes.

entries.clue: Lie low we’re told by Scottish explorer in green space (4,4)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: we hear it rather than read it

blocks.note: to hide is to lie low
Mungo Park, Scottish explorer of the Niger

annotation.surface: Someone lies low beside a Scottish explorer out in some greenery.
annotation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is one of London's great open green spaces.

entries.clue: Might time’s character be so described in Ariosto? (11)

annotation.definition: Might time’s character be so described in Ariosto?

blocks.clueFragment: Might time’s character be so described
blocks.note: reads like asking how Time is portrayed as a figure; in fact 'character' is a letter, T, the symbol for time
in the name ARIOSTO the T is the next-to-last letter, which gives the description

annotation.surface: A scholar wonders how Time itself might be portrayed in the Italian poet Ariosto.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like literary criticism. Read 'character' as a letter: T, the symbol for time, sits second from the end of Ariosto.
annotation.definitionFit: Penultimate means last but one, which is where T stands in Ariosto.

entries.clue: Italian friend crossing delta in kayak? (10)

annotation.definitionNote: kayak is an example of a palindrome, flagged by the question mark

indicatorNotes.crossing: D cuts across the phrase, sitting within it

blocks.note: a friend in Italy: PAL IN ROME
D = delta in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An Italian companion paddles a kayak across a river delta.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian friend' is read as a phrase, PAL IN ROME, and D slots in. Kayak reads the same both ways.
annotation.definitionFit: Kayak spelt backwards is still kayak, so it is a palindrome.

entries.clue: Spooner’s no drink in the pot for this creature? (9)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: swap the opening sounds of two words, as Dr Spooner did

blocks.note: a flagon is a large drinking vessel; it takes the DR sound from its partner
dry = with no drink in it; it takes the FL sound in exchange

annotation.surface: Spooner complains that the jug is empty, and wonders what creature is to blame.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives FLAGON DRY; swapping the first sounds gives DRAGON FLY.
annotation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a large flying insect, a creature.

entries.clue: Rest last of vertebrae in nuchal region (4)

indicatorNotes.last of: takes the final letter of the next word

annotation.surface: An anatomy note: rest the final neck bones in the region at the back of the neck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nuchal' means of the nape, so the definition is the anatomical term.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: 'nuchal' is the anatomist's adjective for the back of the neck.

entries.clue: Continent lives recalled among group forgoing alcohol (4)

indicatorNotes.among: to be among a group is to be in its midst, so the reversed word sits inside

annotation.surface: A temperance group's past lives are remembered by someone continent, or self-restrained.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Continent' can mean self-restrained, which suits the teetotal group; here it is the landmass.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example-of-class: one of the seven landmasses, and the largest.

entries.clue: He’d often check blue pens make the grade (7)

indicatorNotes.pens: SKY encloses PASS as a pen encloses animals

blocks.note: to pass is to make the grade

annotation.surface: A teacher who marks in blue ink checks whether pupils have passed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' is the chess move, not marking; 'pens' is a verb. Boris Spassky was world chess champion 1969-72.
annotation.definitionFit: A chess champion like Spassky often puts the opponent's king in check.

entries.clue: Associate successfully completed replacing outbuilding with church (10)

indicatorNotes.replacing: CE takes the place of SHED

blocks.note: a shed is an outbuilding; it comes out
CE = Church of England; it goes in

annotation.surface: A building project finished once the shed was pulled down and a church put up instead.
annotation.walkthrough: The SHED at the end of ACCOMPLISHED is swapped for CE.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym with a shading: the associate is a partner in crime, not merely a colleague.

entries.clue: That female feeding rook calls for some nuts (7)

indicatorNotes.feeding: feeding goes into a mouth, so the female is put inside the calls

blocks.note: a rook's call is a caw

annotation.surface: A woman feeding a noisy rook finds it squawking for nuts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feeding' looks like giving the bird food; it means going inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'some nuts' names a class, and the kidney-shaped cashew is one member of it.

entries.clue: Yen withdrawn from somehow atypical City resource? (7)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn from: Y is taken out of the word
indicatorNotes.somehow: the rest is arranged in some other way

blocks.note: Y = yen, the Japanese currency; it is removed

annotation.surface: Currency is pulled out of an unusual financial resource in the City.
annotation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose resource is capital; 'City' also suggests a capital city.
annotation.definitionFit: Capital is money, the resource the City of London trades in.

entries.clue: Very keen to grasp fabulous wit (8)

blocks.note: rave = excellent, fabulous, as in rave reviews

annotation.surface: Someone is eager to understand a marvellous piece of wit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very keen to grasp' reads like eager to understand; ravenous is eager to seize food.
annotation.definitionFit: Ravenous means voraciously eager to get hold of something, especially food.

entries.clue: Quarrelsome carpenter (6)

blocks.note: touchy, ready to take offence, as with a chip on the shoulder
British slang for a woodworker, from the chips of wood

annotation.surface: A description of a bad-tempered joiner.
annotation.walkthrough: Chippy is British slang for a carpenter; as an adjective it means touchy, with a chip on the shoulder.
annotation.definitionFit: Chippy means quarrelsome, and it is also slang for a carpenter.

entries.clue: Structures making use of bars belonging to US composer (5)

annotation.surface: Some pieces built from musical bars belong to an American composer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests bars of music, fitting the composer; they are metal bars.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an enclosure built of metal bars, with 'bars' pretending to be musical.

entries.clue: County nuts get near senior NCO (5,8)

indicatorNotes.nuts: crazy, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: Rural nutters close in on a senior non-commissioned officer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a noun (county nutters) but is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A staff sergeant is a non-commissioned officer above a sergeant.

entries.clue: Trouble’s coming up in Parliament (3)

indicatorNotes.coming up: in a down answer, read upwards
indicatorNotes.in: the letters are inside the word

blocks.note: the letters LIA sit inside parLIAment
reversal indicator: in a down answer, the letters are read from the bottom

annotation.surface: Trouble is brewing in Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' reads as an item on the agenda; in a down clue it means read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, now mostly heard in 'what ails you?': to afflict or trouble.

entries.clue: Subordinate action attributed to freedom of movement (2-4)

blocks.note: a work by someone is attributed to them
play = slack, room to move, as in a rope

annotation.surface: A minor act is credited to a policy of free movement.
annotation.walkthrough: Byplay is secondary action on stage going on beside the main plot.
annotation.definitionFit: By-play is subsidiary action, especially on stage.

entries.clue: Weird rites, secretive veils — like nuns perhaps (8)

indicatorNotes.Weird: strange, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.veils: SLY covers the anagram as a veil covers a face

annotation.surface: Strange secret ceremonies and veils, as a convent might hold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Veils' looks like a noun, a nun's headwear; it is the verb, SLY wrapping ISTER.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuns are Sisters, so they behave in a sisterly way; 'perhaps' flags the example.
